evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips directly into confirmation of move date without the 10–15 minute time-box and 'quote you can depend on' framing. Jeline: 'Alright, let's talk about your move. Just to confirm sir you're requested, or your move date is on October 18th which is Sunday.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics confirmation and details without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer during the call.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised, so no reflection opportunity existed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers property type (apartment), floor/stories (third floor pickup, second floor delivery), number of rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (20 feet to elevator, 40 feet from elevator to apartment, 10 feet from parking to staircase at destination), additional rooms (balcony noted), special considerations (sectional couch, bed frame disassembled, dresser, TV stand, shelves). All seven logistics categories addressed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Customer mentions 'we're probably gonna pack most of the up anyways' but rep never proactively asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Not offered by rep.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Jeline: 'Mm-hmm okay, thank you. And normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?' Customer confirms yes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Jeline provides range: '$808 to $1,010 with two movers and one truck' and personalizes it to the specific move logistics: 'the current apartment is on the third floor. Though there's an elevator access we have to consider that there is a possibly long walk and then moving everything into a second floor apartment and the drive time between location could be between thirty minutes to an hour.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep mentions '2.5-hour-minimum' concept indirectly ('time will only start as soon as the team arrives') and explains charging for actual time used, but does NOT explicitly state the trip fee, overnight fee, or packing materials disclosure upfront. Also mentions the $2,000 damage coverage is 'included in the hourly rate' but no explicit 'not a guess' or '15-minute-increments' language.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate. Jeline immediately asks 'So with that, do you have any questions about the pricing or the estimate?' — different framing, no silence hold.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Never mentioned. No reference to starting to discount immediately if late or any on-time guarantee.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Jeline mentions: 'included in the hourly rate is the additional coverage that can cover you up to $2,000 per move. If there are any accidental damages.' This covers the $2,000 and that it's built into the rate, but does NOT explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or any equivalent closing question for the Two Promises section. No loop closure.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Jeline asks 'Do you have any questions before I let you go?' — a throwaway 'any questions?' phrasing, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' before closing.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead, Jeline says 'Okay, thank you and then I'll just send you your final confirmation email that there is a confirmed booking for October 18th.' The booking is assumed, not explicitly asked for.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Never mentioned. No reference to rate lock or price guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Jeline confirms: 'confirmed booking for October 18th. Arrival is between 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM' and mentions follow-up emails and a day-before call. Missing: explicit phone number confirmation, crew size confirmation, and crew notes about customer concerns. Partially confirmed.

top_strength: Thorough and natural logistics discovery — Jeline systematically gathered all seven probing details (property type, floors, room count, walking distances, special items, large furniture) in a conversational flow that felt like genuine fact-finding, not a checklist.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the critical quid pro quo framing (10–15 minute time-box and 'quote you can depend on' promise) — start every call with that frame and wait for the customer's yes before moving into discovery, and Section 2's 'What are your biggest concerns other than price?' is the single most load-bearing omission, as it shapes the entire rest of the call; add it immediately after the initial setup.
